inferred_layout: JAIPUR1_daily.csv: system JAIPUR1; time column 'Date'; interval_energy from ['Energy (kWh)'] in kWh; 1440-minute steps. system_id taken from the file name.
honest_gaps: Tilt and azimuth are not provided by the data source. Daily mode does not use them (the seasonal reference absorbs the orientation), so no value was assumed.
Commissioning date is not provided by the data source; it is not used in any calculation.
Months with too few clear days for their own reference (borrowed from neighbouring months): [7, 8, 12].

reference_method.description: Daily mode. Daily horizontal irradiation × nameplate capacity × a temperature factor (-0.4%/°C, NOCT 45 °C cell-temperature rule). Performance index = measured ÷ modelled energy. The reference is the system's own 90th-percentile sustained (7-clear-day median) performance per calendar month, pooled over all years and reduced by the upward bias expected from noise. Clear day = all-sky ÷ clear-sky irradiation ≥ 0.85. Assumptions: constant inverter and wiring losses are absorbed by the reference; timestamps are local standard time; the cleanest state seen in each month is representative of a clean array.

estimated_loss.interval_method: block bootstrap of clear-day residuals and of the reference

detection_limit.statement: losses below about 9.1% sustained over 14 days, or about 12.0% sustained over 30 days, cannot be distinguished from noise

facts: Output was near zero on 29 day(s) with good irradiance: 2022-09-22; 2022-09-26; 2022-12-05 to 2022-12-31 (27 days).
cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: Near-zero days are consistent with an inverter trip, grid outage or a monitoring fault that recorded zeros. The data cannot tell these apart.

facts: Between cleaning events, performance declined in 2 of 2 usable intervals, at a median of 0.232% per day in the declining ones.
1 of 7 testable natural rain event(s) were followed by a rise in normalised performance that is distinguishable from zero.

rdtools estimates a soiling loss of 5.3% (range 1.3–12.1%, rdtools 3.2.1 stochastic rate and recovery (SRR)). Shuffle check: with the same clear-day values in random time order, which contain no soiling pattern, it reports 6.0–12.4%.
cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: No soiling distinguishable from scatter. The estimate of 5.3% (range 1.3–12.1%, rdtools 3.2.1 stochastic rate and recovery (SRR)) is not clearly above what the same method reports on shuffled data (up to 12.4%), so most or all of it can be produced by day-to-day scatter alone.

facts: Only 1.0 years of data; more than 2 years are needed to separate ageing from seasonal effects.
Cannot be assessed from daily data: shading shows as dips at fixed hours.

inferred_layout: pvdaq_system_1419.csv: system 1419; time column 'measured_on'; cumulative_counter from ['ac_kwhr_1_kwhac__4798', 'ac_kwhr_2_kwhac__4800'] in kWh; 15-minute steps. 2 counters (one per inverter) are summed. sampling interval varies: 15 min on 958 days, 5 min on 453 days.
honest_gaps: 188 day(s) in deep-drop episodes (part of the system off) are excluded from the recovery, soiling, ageing and shading tests, so those tests describe the system while it was otherwise working.

reference_method.description: Hourly mode. NASA POWER hourly global irradiance is split into beam and diffuse (Erbs), transposed to the array plane (Hay-Davies, pvlib) and converted to DC energy with a PVWatts model (temperature coefficient -0.4%/°C, NOCT 45 °C). Hourly values are summed to days. Performance index = measured ÷ modelled energy. The reference is the system's own 90th-percentile sustained (7-clear-day median) performance per calendar month, pooled over all years and reduced by the upward bias expected from noise. Clear day = all-sky ÷ clear-sky irradiation ≥ 0.85. Assumptions: constant inverter and wiring losses are absorbed by the reference; timestamps are local standard time; the cleanest state seen in each month is representative of a clean array.

estimated_loss.interval_method: block bootstrap of clear-day residuals and of the reference

detection_limit.statement: losses below about 5.1% sustained over 14 days, or about 4.0% sustained over 30 days, cannot be distinguished from noise

facts: No day with good irradiance had near-zero output.
186 day(s) have no usable generation data (nothing logged, or a reading missing from at least one inverter); whether the system produced on those days is unknown and they are not counted as loss.

Sustained output was more than 25% below the reference on 188 day(s) (median level 55% of reference): 2016-02-12 to 2016-02-27 (16 days); 2016-09-05 to 2016-10-08 (34 days); 2017-07-25 to 2017-09-07 (45 days); 2019-03-05 to 2019-04-14 (41 days); 2019-07-28 to 2019-07-31 (4 days); 2019-09-02 to 2019-09-10 (9 days); 2019-09-20 to 2019-10-03 (14 days); 2019-11-08 to 2019-12-02 (25 days). This accounts for 15,552 kWh of the sustained shortfall.
cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: The deep sustained drop is consistent with part of the system being off (one inverter, string or meter channel), which is too large and too abrupt for soiling.

facts: Between cleaning events, performance declined in 12 of 12 usable intervals, at a median of 0.349% per day in the declining ones.
0 of 9 testable natural rain event(s) were followed by a rise in normalised performance that is distinguishable from zero.

rdtools estimates a soiling loss of 5.9% (range 3.3–9.1%, rdtools 3.2.1 stochastic rate and recovery (SRR)). Shuffle check: with the same clear-day values in random time order, which contain no soiling pattern, it reports 2.7–5.1%.
cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: No soiling distinguishable from scatter. The estimate of 5.9% (range 3.3–9.1%, rdtools 3.2.1 stochastic rate and recovery (SRR)) is not clearly above what the same method reports on shuffled data (up to 5.1%), so most or all of it can be produced by day-to-day scatter alone.

facts: Year-on-year change of clear-day performance over 4.0 years: -0.44% per year (range -1.00 to +0.13% per year, rdtools 3.2.1 year-on-year).
cause_hypotheses.hypothesis: No ageing trend distinguishable from zero: the range includes zero or is positive.

facts: Clock check: on clear days the measured daily profile is centred +51 minutes from the modelled one (+57 min in May-August, +8 min in November-February).
The timestamps do not line up with solar time well enough for an hour-by-hour test (the summer-winter difference suggests the logger follows daylight-saving time).
